land.text: the realms of Yan Xishan (Shanxi), Feng Yuxiang ('the provinces of Gansu, Shaanxi and Henan') and the Guangxi clique's home province, Guangxi. Hunan is left out: the page's 'Hunan was controlled by the Guangxi clique (in addition to their other lands)' belongs to the lead-up to the 1929 war, and in 1930 Hunan was the Guangxi Army's front, not coalition land

predecessors.note: The cliques were allies inside the Nationalist army until the war (republic-of-china dossier, vassal events of 1930); the coalition took their land out of the Nationalist camp.

land.text: the coalition's land after the resignations of 4 November 1930

successors.note: The page does not say who held Shanxi, Shaanxi or Guangxi after November 1930 (the Shanxi Army withdrew north of the Yellow River (closely paraphrased); the Guangxi Army was forced home (closely paraphrased)); Beijing went to Zhang Xueliang's Northeast Army in September 1930 (a Fengtian-clique realm, no dossier). The republic-of-china dossier carries the Nationalist side.

capitals.name: Beiping (Beijing)
capitals.note: 'The coalition created a new KMT government in Beijing to show their defiance of the Nanjing government.' The page gives neither a date nor a name for it; it fell to Zhang Xueliang's Northeast Army in late September 1930.

correction.text: Shanxi (the Shanxi Army), Shaanxi, Gansu, Guangxi (the Guangxi Army's home province) and the seat of the rival government at Beijing; Henan is not drawn here, it is the guominjun dossier's land; Hunan is not coalition land in 1930 (it is a contest zone, ledger May-November 1930); holds for 1930 only (to 4 November 1930), not 1931

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 556,635 km2 shape (1930-1931) is Shanxi (92% covered), Guangxi (85%), Shaanxi (67%) and a corner of Hebei; it leaves out Henan (2%), Gansu (1%) and Beijing, which the page gives to the coalition. The adjusted shape resolves to 5,100 cells (1.29 M km2 by the gazetteer's cell area) against 2,528 cells (639,331 km2 by the same cell area) for Cliopatria's own shape: 2.0 times by cells, about 1.2 M km2 and about 2.2 times Cliopatria's 556,635 km2 in shapes.csv terms. The page gives no infobox area, so neither figure can be tested. [fix 2026-10-25] An earlier draft added Hunan (about 210,000 km2) on the strength of 'Hunan was controlled by the Guangxi clique', a sentence of the 1929 lead-up; in 1930 the page has the Guangxi Army march north into Hunan, take Yueyang and be cut off and forced home, so Hunan is a front and stays only in the contest zones. The shape also ends too late: the page ends the war on 4 November 1930 ('both Yan Xishan and Feng Yuxiang announced their resignations'), so 1931 should carry no coalition. The Shanxi Army page (Shanxi clique) and the Yan Xishan page were opened and are silent on 1930, so Yan's own land is Shanxi from the army's name, confidence 2. fx-29 (F147): Henan cut (816 cells held by the guominjun dossier, which the coalition's found and keyframe both claimed in 1930): Central Plains War page, 'Feng controlled the provinces of Gansu, Shaanxi and Henan'.

region.text: the realms of Yan Xishan and the Guangxi clique's home province, Feng Yuxiang's Gansu, and the rival government at Beijing; Henan, Feng's land, is left to the guominjun dossier

ledger.note: 1930: Yan Xishan takes the lead of the anti-Chiang coalition. 'Later in the same month [February 1930], Yan assumed the leadership position in the anti-Chiang coalition'; the page dates the coalition's formation to November (1929), when 'Li Zongren issued a declaration to form anti-Chiang coalition along with Wang Jingwei', and Tang Shengzhi and Zhang Fakui joined in December. The page names Feng's realm (Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan) but not Yan's land beyond the Shanxi Army, and gives Hunan to the Guangxi clique only in its 1929 lead-up; the map draws the coalition from Cliopatria's 1930 start. [fix 2026-10-25] Hunan removed from the found region: in 1930 it is the Guangxi Army's front (contest from May, Yueyang below), not coalition land. fx-29 (F147): Henan cut from the found region. The Central Plains War page: 'Feng controlled the provinces of Gansu, Shaanxi and Henan', and the infobox calls the side 'Warlord coalitions of Yan Xishan, Feng Yuxiang and Li Zongren': Henan is a member's land, which the guominjun dossier already holds since 28 May 1927 (/ledger/7, Luoyang), so both dossiers drew the same 816 cells and the compiler gave them to one side at the found and to the other at the keyframe.

region.text: the fronts of the second phase: Kaifeng in Henan, Jinan in Shandong, Yueyang in Hunan, Gansu and Shaanxi

ledger.note: 11 May 1930: Chiang's Central Army opens the general offensive. 'On 11 May, the Central Army led by Chiang Kai-shek launched a series of general offensives'; it reached the outskirts of Kaifeng by 16 May and was crushed by the Northwest Army in Gansu by the end of May. The infobox dates the second phase May-November 1930.

Before 25 June 1930 (page silent on the date): the Guangxi Army takes Yueyang. 'In the southern battlefields the Guangxi Army led by Li Zongren and Bai Chongxi marched northwards and captured Yueyang' (page, closely paraphrased); the sentence stands in the 1930 narrative just before 'In Shandong the Shanxi Army captured Jinan on 25 June', the stretch carries no year of its own and joins the Jinan dates the ledger gives to 1930, so June is the latest month the page allows and the month here is a bridge, not a date. The Yan Xishan page, opened to date it, is silent.
25 June 1930: the Shanxi Army takes Jinan. The page: the Shanxi Army captured Jinan, Shandong, on 25 June, and Chiang's forces retook it on 15 August (closely paraphrased).

Before 15 August 1930 (page silent on the date): the Guangxi Army is cut off and forced home. 'Chiang's forces managed to cut them off from behind, eventually forcing them to withdraw to their home province' and 'After defeating the Guangxi Army in Hunan, the Nanjing government decided to launch a major counteroffensive against the Shanxi Army in Shandong' (page, closely paraphrased), which comes before 'Chiang's forces retook Jinan on 15 August'; August is the latest month the page allows and is a bridge, not a date.
15 August 1930: Jinan is retaken. Chiang's forces retook Jinan on 15 August (page, closely paraphrased).

region.text: Peking, held by the coalition's Beijing government and entered by the Northeast Army

ledger.note: Late September 1930: Zhang Xueliang takes Peking. On 18 September he and the Northeast Army 'abandoned their neutrality and declared their support for Chiang'; 'several days later the Northeast Army entered the North China Plain through Shanhai Pass and captured Peking two days later'. The page gives no exact date for the capture. [review ea-08-d 2026-10-25] Counterpart set to the slug of the fengtian-clique dossier (ea-08-x), which now exists.

region.text: the fronts of the second phase

ledger.note: 4 November 1930: the war ends. 'On 4 November both Yan Xishan and Feng Yuxiang announced their resignations from all of their positions', which effectively ended hostilities; the infobox ends the war in November 1930.

region.text: the coalition's land: Shanxi, Shaanxi, Gansu, Henan and Guangxi (with Beijing already lost in September)

ledger.note: 4 November 1930: the coalition collapses. Yan and Feng resign; the page says the Shanxi Army withdrew north of the Yellow River (closely paraphrased) and the Guangxi Army was cut off at Yueyang and forced home (closely paraphrased). It does not say who held Shanxi, Shaanxi or Guangxi afterwards, so the land is returned to the Nationalist Republic (as its provinces and former allies) at confidence 2.

wars.name: Central Plains War

zones.text: Kaifeng and Henan, Jinan and Shandong, Yueyang and Hunan, Gansu and Shaanxi

wars.outcome: Nationalist government victory: Yan Xishan and Feng Yuxiang resigned on 4 November 1930 and the Beiping government fell once Zhang Xueliang's Northeast Army declared for Chiang (18 September) and took Peking.
wars.note: The page dates the whole war March 1929 to November 1930 (first phase March-November 1929, the Autumn War from September 1929, second phase May-November 1930, the offensive of 11 May); the coalition row covers only the 1930 phase. The 1929 revolts (Guangxi clique in March 1929, Feng Yuxiang in May 1929) are before Cliopatria's start and have no shape.

certainty.note: Provincial lines of the cliques' realms, not survey borders; the fronts (Kaifeng, Jinan, Yueyang) moved month by month and the page gives no boundary.

sources.title: Central Plains War
sources.note: Dates (March 1929 to November 1930), the realms of Feng Yuxiang and the Guangxi clique, Yan's leadership in February 1930, the Beijing government, the dated fronts, 4 November 1930.

sources.title: Shanxi clique
sources.note: Opened for Yan Xishan's land and the Beiping government; thin: it says nothing of 1930-1931 (infobox allegiance 'Nationalist government (1927-1929; 1930-1949)'), so no event rests on it.

sources.title: Yan Xishan
sources.note: Opened in the repair pass for the date of the Beijing government and of Yueyang; silent on both (only: Chiang's defeat of Yan and Feng in 1930 ended the Warlord Era; Time cover of 19 May 1930). No event rests on it.

notes: Budget 1-2 pages: Central Plains War (all events) and Shanxi clique (thin, nothing used). RAISED FOR THE REVIEWER: (1) Cliopatria's 1930-1931 row is Shanxi, Guangxi and Shaanxi only; the page also gives the coalition Gansu, Henan, Hunan and a government at Beijing, and ends the war on 4 November 1930, so 1931 is dropped; the adjusted shape (about 1.2 M km2, 5,100 cells against Cliopatria's 2,528, about 2.2 times its 556,635 km2) is bigger than Cliopatria's and no infobox figure exists to test it. Hunan is NOT in it: the page's 'Hunan was controlled by the Guangxi clique' is a sentence of the 1929 lead-up (repair pass 2026-10-25); in 1930 Hunan is the Guangxi Army's front (contest zones; Yueyang gain and loss at confidence 1). (2) The page does not date the Beijing government or name Yan Xishan's land: Shanxi is from 'Shanxi Army'; Beijing is the page's. The Yan Xishan page (opened in the repair pass) is silent on both the government's date and Yueyang's. (3) The coalition's formation is November 1929 on the page (Li Zongren and Wang Jingwei) and the war began in March 1929; the dossier starts in February 1930 with Yan's leadership and Cliopatria's year. (4) Mirror events: the republic-of-china dossier has the matching contest_start (May 1930) and contest_end (November 1930) but no gain from this coalition in November 1930 and no loss of Beijing to Zhang Xueliang in September 1930; the Guangxi clique, Guominjun, Shanxi clique and Fengtian clique have no dossiers (names used as counterparts). (5) Wikidata Q717809 is the war's item. No gazetteer names are missing.
